title: Canonical pro-etale supported exterior product and finite-coefficient presentation
statement:
Use the small pro-etale sites and constant coefficient modules of
[def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], their derived categories and derived tensor
[def-weil-derived-tensor], and the closed support functors of
[def-pur-support-cohomology]. Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring, let $B,X,Y,Z,W$
be schemes, and let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$, $j:W\hookrightarrow Y$ be closed
immersions [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Suppose $X,Y$ are locally Noetherian and
$f:X\to B$, $g:Y\to B$ have locally Noetherian fibre product
$P=X\times_B Y$ [def-pc-base-change]. Write $p:P\to X$, $q:P\to Y$ for its
projections and $h=i\times_B j:Z\times_B W\to P$.

For an $A$-module $M$, define $C_i(M)=i_*\underline M_Z$ and the quotient
$q_i:\underline M_X\to C_i(M)$ by the constant-sheaf inverse-image identification
and the inverse-image/direct-image adjunction. This exact functor is left adjoint
to $\Gamma_Z$. Fix this adjunction uniquely by requiring, for every sheaf $F$ and
map $a:M\to\Gamma_Z(F)$, that its adjoint precomposed with $q_i$ equals the
constant-sheaf adjoint of $a$ followed by the kernel inclusion
$\Gamma_Z(F)\to\Gamma(X,F)$. Derive this exact-left/right-derived adjunction to
obtain $C_i:D(A)\to D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ left adjoint to $R\Gamma_Z$, and
likewise for $j,h$.

For $A$-modules $M,N$, fix
$\theta:C_h(M\otimes_A N)\to p^*C_i(M)\otimes_A q^*C_j(N)$ uniquely by its
composite with $q_h$: the constant-section tensor pairing followed by
$p^*q_i\otimes_A q^*q_j$. On signed total complexes fix the chain map by this
map on every $(r,s)$ summand with $r+s=n$. Localize using K-flat complexes; fix
the derived comparison uniquely by naturality in both variables and compatibility
with the tensor-localization comparison on every pair of cochain representatives.
For $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ and $L\in D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ define
$$
\kappa^{Z,W}_{K,L}:R\Gamma_ZK\otimes_A^L R\Gamma_WL
\longrightarrow R\Gamma_h(K\boxtimes_A^L L)
$$
as the adjoint of the derived $\theta$ followed by the tensor of the pulled-back
evaluation counits. This is the pro-etale analogue of
[def-pur-supported-exterior-product].

The canonical finite-coefficient realization from fixed $A$-module sheaves to
modules over the associated constant ring sheaf [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]
is an exact equivalence. Its derived inverse supplies the fixed-ring presentation
of each specified etale-origin realization [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness].
For schemes locally of finite type over a field [def-weil-finite-type-morphism],
use the same $\kappa$, deriving the locally Noetherian instances from the structure
maps.

proof.text: For elaboration of the derived functors, supportedSheaf_intColimitsGeneric proves existence of integer-indexed colimits of sheaves directly with Mathlib Sheaf.instHasColimitsOfShape. Register it only as a local instance. It replaces repeated general colimit-shrinking searches by a single proved proposition and introduces no mathematical choice or new data. The companion supportedSheaf_smallColimitsGeneric supplies all small-shaped colimits directly from Sheaf.instHasColimitsOfShape, so cochain tensor instances do not repeatedly shrink general colimit universes.

Auxiliary complex-tensor identity: supportedComplexTensorGeneric is the upstream curried tensor on cochain complexes, whose object is definitionally HomologicalComplex.tensorObj, exactly supportedTotalTensorGeneric. Reflexivity proves supportedComplexTensorGeneric_eq without using flat resolutions. Its existing flat-resolution parameter is retained for interface compatibility.

Construct the ordinary adjunction by composing the constant-sheaf adjunction and the closed lowerStar/closedUpperShriek adjunction. Identify closedUpperShriek followed by lowerStar with sectionsWithSupport using the supported-sheaf equivalence. Compare global sections with the raw kernel of restriction to the complement: the normalized counit and the global restriction unit identify their kernel cones. This proves the required quotient normalization. The quotient is epimorphic because its restriction to the closed subset is invertible and its target is zero on the complement; use complementary restriction zero detection. Cancel this epimorphism to prove uniqueness of the adjunction.

Exactness of supported coefficients now follows from the proved ordinary adjunction for finite colimits, and left exactness of constantSheaf and lowerStar for finite limits. Derive this adjunction using the existing exact-left/right-derived adjunction construction.

Construct the coefficient tensor map by factorization through the closed-support unit. Its target vanishes off the product support: the complement is the union of the two projection inverse images of the separate complements, and on each piece one tensor factor is zero. Detect zero using the actual two-open covering sieve on the pro-etale site, not only set-theoretic surjectivity. The unit is invertible on this supported target. Its adjunction factorization gives existence, and the epimorphic quotient gives uniqueness. Naturality follows by cancellation of that quotient.

Apply the unique signed-complex extension to the natural coefficient comparison. The constant supported coefficient functor preserves coproducts because it is a left adjoint. Identify the chosen complex map with the natural comparison by its summand characterization.

Supported coefficients preserve flat objects: constant sheafification preserves flatness and closed direct image preserves flatness. Projection inverse image also preserves flatness. Apply the derived comparison theorem to G=C_h, F₁=p* C_i, F₂=q* C_j and the proved natural complex comparison. The shared interfaces preserve the original morphism types, naturality maps and model equation.

Identify the explicit derived-tensor bifunctor presentation with externalProduct. Both use the two projection inverse images and the same existing monoidal structure. Prove the generic tensor object identity and the externalProduct identity separately, using structural heterogeneous congruence for category-instance data so the kernel need not repeatedly unfold the large derived monoidal construction. Compose these equalities. No tensor structure, target or supported exterior-product definition is replaced.

proof_origin.place: Ordinary support adjunction, coefficient tensor, signed complex extension, K-flat descent; all five original holes proved. Preserve W4’s auxiliary proofs and the existing supported exterior product construction.

lean.statement: def supportedExteriorProductOverField (A : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing A] [Finite A] (k : Type u) [Field k] {X Y Z W : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) (g : Y ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [LocallyOfFiniteType g] (i : Z ⟶ X) (j : W ⟶ Y) [IsClosedImmersion i] [IsClosedImmersion j] (K : DerivedCategory (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A))) (L : DerivedCategory (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology Y) (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A))) : (supportedSectionsDerived A i).obj K ⊗ (supportedSectionsDerived A j).obj L ⟶ (supportedSectionsDerived A (Etale.supportedProductImmersion f g i j)).obj (externalProduct (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) f g K L)
